name: ASUS router (AiMesh)
description: Reads which device is connected to which AiMesh node (stock ASUSWRT, tested on an RT-AX92U) for the hierarchy and the map, the router's Traffic Analyzer (traffic per application and per device), and the health of the router and every node: processor, memory, temperature, uptime, firmware, ports and interface speeds (internet, LAN, Wi-Fi). Read-only, never SSH: one login per router, a few reads and a logout per sync. A refused login pauses automatic syncing.
author: Netlens

releases.changelog: Record configuration changes also reads the second DHCP DNS server, so Netlens can tell a single resolver from two (one more small request per sync, only with the option on). Nothing changes while the option is off. Needs Netlens 0.4.387.

Record configuration changes: the router answers only the first setting of a request, so every setting is now asked on its own (about 45 small requests per sync, only with this option on). Nothing changes while the option is off. Needs Netlens 0.4.387.
The diagnostic has a new configuration_names step: which setting names the router answers (names only, never values), in groups and one by one. Nothing else changed. Needs Netlens 0.4.387.

New setting Record configuration changes (off by default): the plugin reads a fixed list of the router's settings (firewall, UPnP, remote access, DHCP, DNS, Wi-Fi security, VPN, port forwards; never passwords or keys) and Netlens tells what changed. Read-only; a failed read never fails the sync. Run diagnostic has a new configuration step. Nothing changes while the setting is off. Needs Netlens 0.4.387.

Talks to the device through Netlens' shared HTTP client (certificate and host name checks, timeouts, size limit and redirect rules are the same in every plugin). Needs Netlens 0.4.366 or newer. No change in what the plugin reads or writes.

The health of the main router and of every AiMesh node: processor, memory, temperature, uptime, firmware (and the update that is waiting), the physical ports (cable and speed) and the speed of the interfaces (internet, wired, Wi-Fi radios), read with the main router's login at the address the router lists for each node. Nothing to set up per node; switches in the plugin settings turn it off. Includes the interface speeds planned as 1.4.0. Needs Netlens 0.4.237.

Application statistics per device: the 25 busiest devices of today also get their own application list (one extra request each), shown on the device's Network tab. Honours the new switch Settings > Traffic statistics in Netlens 0.4.161 (off by default; while off the router is not asked). Needs Netlens 0.4.161.

Reads the router's Traffic Analyzer when it is on: bytes per application and per device for today and yesterday, shown in Statistics > Applications (needs Netlens 0.4.154 or newer). New setting Read the Traffic Analyzer statistics (on by default); models without the Traffic Analyzer pages are skipped. Nothing else changed.
Now an ordinary plugin (it was built into Netlens before 0.4.44). Same code as the built-in version 1.1.0; Netlens installs it again by itself for existing setups.
